verdict.line: You win the early trades and the all-in race before 6, but the 45.4% head-to-head win rate over 152 games says stacked Siphoning Strike and Fury of the Sands take the game back from you if it goes long.

brief.thesis: Nasus has no gap closer and a 255-range Q (Siphoning Strike), so mini Gnar's ranged Q (Boomerang Throw) and kiting win nearly every trade before level 6. The problem is Siphoning Strike's bonus damage is permanent per minion kill, and R (Fury of the Sands) at 6 gives him health, range, and health drain on demand — so lane advantage and solo-kill advantage are real, but they don't erase the long-game scaling that explains the sub-50% win rate.

theirWindow.what: Fury of the Sands gives him bonus health, attack range, cast range, and max-health drain for its duration — don't commit to extended trades here, and keep Hop (E) ready to disengage rather than stand and fight.

yourWindow.what: Poke with Q (Boomerang Throw) at its 1100 range and proc Hyper (W) on autos; Nasus has nothing to punish you at range, so force him to either farm passively or walk into bad trades.

start.why: 50.8% win rate over 126 games as the clear preferred start — the extra sustain lets you keep landing Q pokes in extended trades without backing off.

boots.why: 50% win rate over 62 games; flat physical damage reduction blunts both his auto-attacks and Siphoning Strike as his stacks grow.

runes.keystoneWhy: 48% win rate and the higher-pick page of the two viable keystones — the move speed and heal on hit-and-run attacks directly reward kiting a melee champion with no gap closer. Master-tier players instead run Lethal Tempo (1,803 games); that suits a more aggressive, attack-speed-stacking playstyle that commits to prolonged trades rather than poke-and-disengage.

summoners.why: 51.4% win rate, the best of the three recorded pages — it converts your early solo-kill advantage into an actual kill before his stacks and R come online. Flash+Teleport (67.2% pick rate) is the more popular choice if you'd rather play for scaling and side-lane pressure instead.

playing.title: Poke at max Q range
playing.detail: Boomerang Throw (Q) reaches 1100 range and slows on hit; throw it before he's in his own Q range so every trade before 6 is free damage.

playing.title: Contest his Siphoning Strike farm
playing.detail: Each minion Siphoning Strike kills permanently increases its damage, so pushing him off last hits or trading when he goes for a cannon minion directly slows his scaling.

playing.title: Disengage once R is up
playing.detail: From level 6 on, Fury of the Sands gives him bonus health, range, and max-health drain for its duration; use Hop (E) to leave rather than trade through it.

playing.title: Track his Wither cooldown
playing.detail: Wither (W) is 15/14/13/12/11s and cuts your move and attack speed; once he burns it, you have a clean window to all-in or disengage before it's back up.

playing.title: Save Mega Gnar transform for his all-in
playing.detail: Transforming at max Rage gives you Wallop (W), a stun — time it for when he commits Wither or R so you punish the engage instead of eating it.

playing.title: Step off Spirit Fire
playing.detail: Spirit Fire (E) reduces armor in its area; standing in it lets his Q and autos hit harder than the trade should allow, so back out of the zone before continuing to fight.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win rates/sample sizes above are measured from current-patch games on OP.GG; the matchup reasoning, timing windows, and ability interactions are my own tactical read.

stats.opponentTip: Use Unflinching or Mercury’s Treads to deal with (W) while kiting him often to gain control over lane. Be careful of being killed when he reaches level 6.
